messages:
marta: Quick check — after merging the batch-scheduler tweak (sha: f3a2b9c) we're seeing a tail latency bump on 16k tokens in the paged-attn CI runs. Can someone run a focused profiling sweep?

rahul: I can run a sweep on the nvlink cluster. Which harness + config?

marta: Use smokebench-v3 (repo: infra/bench), config `batch_bus=true, max_batch=64, staged_kv=true`. Also flip `fused_ops=true` and `flash_attn_variant=1` to repro. Exact command: `./bench/run --suite smokebench-v3 --config batch_bus=true,max_batch=64,staged_kv=true,fused_ops=true,flash_attn_variant=1 --tokens 16000 --reps 6`

lee: note: if you hit the cold-KV path, add `--kv-warmup 2` to the command so results aren't noisy.

rahul: running now on node gpu-12 (A100-80G), will attach nvprof/trace. ETA ~25m.

jen: FYI I left a small revert branch (marta/revert-sched) that drops the scheduling heuristic; if this is noisy we can quickly switch the canary to that.

marta: thanks. Also pay attention to p99 vs median. The concern is a few large outliers during steady-state when many micro-batches hit the same shard.

ops-bot: deploy: canary started for cluster "staging-inference" (tag: batch-scheduler-f3a2b9c). Monitoring routes: /v1/text and /v1/chat.

rahul: first run done. Median token/sec looks fine (+2%), but p99 latency bumped ~18% for long sequences. nvprof trace attached: `trace_2198765432_nvprof.tar.gz` (uploaded to /tmp/bench-traces).

lee: checking trace: I see kernel serialization around the attention-kv flush; looks like two kernels are queuing back-to-back on the same SMs instead of overlapping. Possibly a launch-order dependency introduced by `batch_bus`'s stream-affinity.

marta: that matches my local repro. The stream-affinity change stashes batches to a single stream to improve caching but can reduce concurrency for paged attention. We might need to relax affinity when `staged_kv=true` is set.

jen: small triage proposal: 1) Rah run a second sweep with `batch_bus=loose` (new flag) or remove affinity, 2) if p99 improves, promote marta/revert-sched as quick rollback, 3) open a follow-up PR to make affinity adaptive. Who owns?

marta: I'll own the adaptive fix. For now let's test `batch_bus=loose`. rahul, can you rerun with `batch_bus=loose,max_batch=64` and same other flags?

rahul: starting rerun now. Command used: `./bench/run --suite smokebench-v3 --config batch_bus=loose,max_batch=64,staged_kv=true,fused_ops=true,flash_attn_variant=1 --tokens 16000 --reps 6 --kv-warmup 2`

ops-bot: bench: run queued on gpu-7.

rahul: second run complete. p99 regression reduced to +3% vs baseline (within noise), median unchanged. Uploading traces: `trace_2198765432_nvprof_loose.tar.gz` to /tmp/bench-traces.

lee: sanity check: verify no change in throughput variance across shards. I scanned the logs, shard imbalance lowered with loose affinity.

marta: great — sounds like a safe revert if needed. Jen, can you flip the canary back to revert branch if ops wants to roll back?

jen: yes. I'll hold off for one hour to let monitoring settle. If no new regressions, we'll mark this as accepted and merge an adaptive affinity PR from marta into staging next week.

marta: I'll open the PR with tests (microbench harness + deterministic trace assertion) and a short doc explaining the heuristics.

rahul: added a short note in the bench run artifact with commands and env. If anyone needs the raw nvprof slices ping me.

lee: thanks all. Quick follow-up: I can prototype adaptive stream selection (heuristic: if staged_kv && avg_batch_size>32 then affinity=loose else affinity=strict) and add a feature flag. Will send a draft by EOD.

marta: perfect. Closing loop: rahul/ops-bot — please keep the run artifacts for 3 days. Tagging this thread as resolved unless new signals show up. :white_check_mark:
